comparisons.peer_topic: Indefinite Reinvestment of Non-U.S. Subsidiary Earnings
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company provides income taxes on book over tax basis differences of non-U.S. subsidiaries unless indefinitely reinvested. At December 31, 2024, $5.8 billion of such differences were indefinitely reinvested, and reversing this assertion would require an additional $2.3 billion in taxes net of U.S. FTCs.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and C disclose the indefinite reinvestment of foreign subsidiary earnings and quantify the hypothetical tax liability if that assertion were reversed. MS reports an unrecognized deferred tax liability of $405 million, whereas C reports that reversing its indefinite reinvestment assertion for $5.8 billion in basis differences would require $2.3 billion in additional taxes net of U.S. FTCs.

sentences.text: The earnings of certain foreign subsidiaries and affiliates are indefinitely reinvested due to regulatory and other capital requirements in foreign jurisdictions.
As of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, the unrecognized deferred tax liability attributable to indefinitely reinvested earnings is $405 million and $302 million, respectively.
The Company provides income taxes on the book over tax basis differences of non-U.S. subsidiaries except to the extent that such differences are indefinitely reinvested outside the U.S.
At the existing tax rates (including withholding taxes), additional taxes (net of U.S. FTCs) of $2.3 billion would have to be provided if such assertions were reversed.

comparisons.peer_summary: The firm permanently reinvested eligible earnings of certain foreign subsidiaries, with all U.S. taxes accrued on these subsidiaries' distributable earnings as of December 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS address the reinvestment of foreign earnings, but they differ fundamentally in their tax provision stance. MS asserts indefinite reinvestment resulting in an unrecognized deferred tax liability of $405 million, while GS permanently reinvests earnings but has accrued all U.S. taxes on these subsidiaries' distributable earnings, resulting in no unrecognized liability for this purpose.
